queries: SELECT tick, year, month, road_maintenance_budget, income_tax_rate, property_tax_rate, electricity_tariff, transit_fare, zoning_release, power_contract_mode FROM lever_monthly JOIN ticks USING (run_id,tick) ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, AVG(wear) AS mean_wear, AVG(congestion) AS mean_congestion, AVG(traffic) AS mean_traffic FROM road_monthly GROUP BY tick ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 12
SELECT tick, income_tax_revenue, property_tax_revenue, utility_revenue, transit_revenue, road_spend, water_sewer_spend, balance, debt, treasury FROM budget_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6
SELECT tick, demand_kw, supply_kw, outage_fraction, contract_mode, tariff FROM power_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6
SELECT tick, capacity, demand, load_ratio, failure_rate FROM water_monthly ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6

SELECT tick, AVG(satisfaction) AS satisfaction, AVG(disposable_income) AS disposable_income, AVG(travel_time) AS travel_time, AVG(CASE WHEN employed THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS employment FROM citizen_monthly LEFT JOIN commute_monthly USING (run_id,tick,citizen_id) GROUP BY tick ORDER BY tick DESC LIMIT 6
turns.rationale: The failing system is clearly the road network: mean wear has risen steadily from 0.80 at tick 49 to 0.969, while maintenance spending has been zero throughout. Congestion is already 0.78, consistent with deteriorating capacity. The city has ample treasury and roughly 655k/month surplus, so I am funding the maximum annual road-maintenance allocation to arrest the immediate infrastructure failure. I am not spending on water, where failure is zero, or changing unrelated levers.
